rows.why: S1 needs the parser to accept every unit, days included ('2d', '1d0h0m0s0ms'). Item 1 asks which units are allowed, and its pick accepts d, h, m, s and ms. Zero being valid (item 7) also fits, but the scenario turns mainly on days being accepted.
Item 5 asks whether whitespace is accepted. The scenario trims whitespace around the value and parses '  45m\n'. The pick rejects whitespace and does no trimming.

Items 3 and 4 also cover some rows. Item 5 covers the most: the empty string, signs, inner whitespace, uppercase units and the full-width digit. It rejects all of them, which matches the scenario's ValueError.
No item asks whether one component can exceed the size of the next unit up, as in '90m'. Item 2 is about unit order and repeats, which is a different behaviour.

Item 2 asks whether units must be in descending order and whether a unit can repeat. The pick allows each unit once, in descending order only, and rejects '30s1m' and '1h1h'. That matches the scenario.
Item 8 asks about the upper limit. The pick rejects only totals above 2^53-1, so exactly 9007199254740991 parses, as the scenario expects.
Item 8's pick rejects totals above 9007199254740991 ms with a ValueError. That matches rejecting 'max+1ms' and the very large ms value.

Item 9 asks how a duration is printed back. The scenario expects a breakdown from largest unit down (5400000 → '1h30m', 90000 → '1m30s'). The pick takes the shortest string and gives '90m'. Zero also differs: item 10's pick gives '0s', but the scenario expects '0ms'.
The scenario wants the largest-to-smallest form '104249991d8h59m991ms' (20 characters). Shortest-string choice would pick a shorter form such as '9007199254740991ms' (18 characters) instead.
No item asks whether formatting then parsing gives the number back. Any of the printing choices in items 9 and 10 would round-trip, so none of them settles this scenario.

Item 11 asks which inputs format_duration rejects. The pick raises ValueError for negatives, values above 2^53-1, bool and float, which matches all four rows. The pick does not say what the error message is, so it does not confirm the scenario's 'milliseconds' wording.
